title: Normalized slice evaluation for continuous coefficient inverse image
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For any scheme $W$, use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the continuous coefficient sheaves $A_W(V)=C(|V|,A)$, $E_W(V)=C(|V|,E)$ with constant-section normalization [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients, lem-weil-pbc-continuous-ring-functions-sheaf]. For a noetherian finite-dimensional $X$ with $\ell$ invertible these identify with $B_X=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_X$ and $B_X[1/\varpi]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. Let $u:U\to X$ be any object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with no noetherian hypothesis on $U$. Under the localization equivalence $U_{\mathrm{proet}}\simeq X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], the inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is canonically the slice restriction $F|_U(V\to U)=F(V\to X)$. It sends the continuous integral and rational coefficient rings to $A_U,E_U$, identically on the continuous functions of the same underlying $V$. It preserves every finite constant quotient, its quotient transitions and the coefficient projections. In the inverse-image indexing category $\mathcal I_V$ this identification is induced by the initial object $(V\to X,(s,\mathrm{id}_V))$, where $s:V\to U$ is the structure map; thus it is normalized for the actual inverse-image construction, including its sheafification. Module restriction is exact and its derived functor is termwise restriction [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence]. In particular, for an etale morphism $g:X'\to X$ between schemes with the same hypotheses the finite-quotient structural maps are isomorphisms $g^{-1}B_X\cong B_{X'}$, $g^{-1}E_X\cong E_{X'}$, and $E_{X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}E_X}g^{-1}(-)$ is exact ordinary inverse image. The same conclusion holds for a locally closed immersion by the specified immersion coefficient isomorphisms. Site restriction of an ambient derived pullback is the corresponding restricted module pullback; all these identifications preserve coefficient maps and constant sections.

proof.text: Use the actual object inverse-image/restriction comparison. The graph-mate evaluation identifies its continuous coefficient map with the canonical pullback on the same continuous functions. Naturality gives coefficient postcomposition and constant-section normalization.

For each finite coefficient quotient, the canonical constant comparison is invertible by pro-etale profinite coefficient inverse image. Its naturality gives transitions; the constant-to-continuous comparison and adjunction naturality identify residue projections. The same naturality gives the integral-to-rational inclusion.

The continuous residue cone is a limit. Transport its unique comparison to the chosen finite-constant-sheaf limit across the discrete-continuous coefficient isomorphism. The localization theorem supplies the normalized rational comparison. Conjugating coefficient pullback by these comparisons gives completed pullback and its projection equations.

Literal module restriction is additive by the sectionwise formula. Its underlying presheaf functor preserves finite limits and reflects them; cocontinuity of composition with a pro-etale object gives its left-adjoint property and hence preservation of colimits. The generic graph mate and the map/pullback adjunction identify this exact restriction with the chosen module inverse image by uniqueness of left adjoints, with the canonical unit on sections. Map the comparison to complexes and derived categories; the standard derived comparison square gives the required normalization.

Scalar extension along a ring-sheaf isomorphism is restriction along its inverse, with the specified pure tensor formula. Transfer exactness across this isomorphism. Uniqueness of the left derived functor of an exact functor supplies its derived comparison with the canonical counit. The ordinary pullback identification and derived composition give ExactPull. For etale maps use their pro-etale site object, and for immersions use the existing continuous coefficient pullback isomorphism.

Apply the generic normalized scalar-extension/slice comparison separately to integral and rational coefficient rings. Its ordinary, section, complex, derived and counit fields give Ambient directly; this is a genuinely coefficient-independent part of the argument.

proof_origin.place: Original normalized slice argument; Lean implementation N4: exact module restriction by limits and adjoints, scalar isomorphism via the existing ring-isomorphism API, completion by the residue limit, ambient comparison through the separate generic scalar/slice theorem.
